title: Inner Critic Courtroom
summary: A role play in which a client puts the inner critic on trial and examines its evidence.
goal: Use it to help a client weigh a harsh voice.
body_md: Set up roles for a prosecutor, a defense and a judge, all played by the client with you assisting. Look at the evidence for and against each critical claim. The client delivers the verdict in their own words. Keep it light and let the client set the pace.

fields.label: What the critic says
Its evidence
The defense's evidence
The verdict
What I will say next time it speaks

title: Self-Worth Without Conditions Practice
summary: A practice for noticing conditions placed on self-worth and acting on values anyway.
goal: Use it to loosen if-then rules about worth.
body_md: Ask what rules the client holds for being okay, such as I must succeed. Look at how well they serve. Practice acting on values without waiting for the rule to be satisfied. Welcome whatever comes up.

fields.label: A rule I hold about being worthy
Where I learned it
What it costs
What I would do without the rule
One step I will take

title: Self-Respect Check-In
summary: A check-in on whether a recent choice fit the client's values and self-respect.
goal: Use it to build choices that leave a client feeling good about themselves.
body_md: Look at a recent interaction and ask what would have helped the client feel proud of how they acted. Role play the response. Keep judgments gentle. The client decides what matters to them.

fields.label: A recent interaction
How I acted
What I value in how I treat others and myself
What I could do next time
How I will remind myself

title: Compliment Mirror Circle
summary: A group game in which each person receives specific compliments and practices simply saying thank you.
goal: Use it to practice receiving kindness.
body_md: Each person gets a turn to hear a specific compliment from others and say thank you without deflecting. Keep it genuine and not generic. Allow passing. In the debrief ask how it felt to receive.

fields.label: A compliment I received
How hard it was to take in
What I said back
A compliment I gave
What I will remember

title: Social Energy Planner
summary: A planner for scheduling social time so a client has recovery time before and after.
goal: Use it to help a client pace social events.
body_md: Look at the client's week and plan which events matter most. Add recovery time after. Avoid using it to cut out all social contact. Tie events to what the client values.

fields.label: Social events this week
Which ones matter most to me
How I will recover
What I will do to prepare
What I will do if it feels like too much

title: Spotlight Reality Check
summary: An experiment for comparing how much a client thinks others notice them with what happens.
goal: Use it to test the spotlight effect.
body_md: Predict how much others will notice a small slip and then run it. Gather reports from a friend or from observations. Compare. The result informs what the client believes. Debrief what was learned.

fields.label: What I think others will notice
How sure I am, 0 to 100
What I tried
What actually happened
What I make of it

title: Showing Up Anyway Practice
summary: A practice for choosing a social action that fits a value while anxiety is present.
goal: Use it to link social steps to what matters.
body_md: Ask what the client would want from social life if anxiety were less in charge. Choose a step and agree to bring anxiety along. Check in on what the experience was like.

fields.label: What I want from my social life
A step that fits
What anxiety says about it
What I will do while it is there
How I will know I did it

title: Social Event Teamwork Plan
summary: A plan for how partners work as a team at social events.
goal: Use it to give a socially anxious partner a supportive plan.
body_md: Ask the more anxious partner what helps and what to avoid, such as being pushed or left alone. Plan a signal for a break and a time to leave. Review afterward and adjust. Respect both partners' needs.

fields.label: Partner A: what helps me at events
Partner B: how I can help
A signal for a break
When we will leave
How we will debrief

title: Brave Conversation Spinner Game
summary: A child spins a spinner for a conversation challenge and practices it with a parent.
goal: Use it to make small social risks playful for a child.
body_md: Make a spinner with challenges like say hello, ask a question or share a favorite. The child spins and the parent plays the other person. Cheer attempts and never speak for the child. Move to real small tries later. Ask the child which spin felt easiest and which felt hardest.

fields.label: The challenge I spun
What I said
How it felt in my body
The spin that was hardest
Who I could try one with this week

title: Grief Memory Collection Sheet
summary: A sheet for collecting small memories and details of someone who has died.
goal: Use it to help a client keep the person close in a gentle way.
body_md: Invite memories of everyday things, such as a laugh or a saying. Let the client set the pace and stop when needed. Some memories may bring tears, which is normal. Offer ways to keep the memories.

fields.label: A small thing I remember about them
A saying or sound I connect to them
Something they taught me
A place I feel close to them
How I want to keep this memory

title: Grief Thought Check Sheet
summary: A thought record for should-have thoughts after a loss.
goal: Use it to look at guilt and what-if thoughts after a death.
body_md: Notice the what-ifs and ask what the client knew then. Hindsight changes the picture. Not every thought should be challenged; some express love. Go gently. The client decides which thoughts to look at.

fields.label: A should-have thought
What I knew at the time
What I would say to a friend
What the thought says about how much I cared
What I want to do with it

title: Carrying Love and Loss Practice
summary: A practice for making room for sorrow while turning toward what the loved person valued.
goal: Use it to hold grief and love together.
body_md: Ask what the person cared about and how the client could honor it. Allow sadness to be present. Avoid hurrying the grief. Pick a small act the client can do this week.

fields.label: Something I miss most
A value they lived by
A way I could honor it
What sadness feels like in my body
What I will do this week

title: Anniversary Cope Ahead Plan
summary: A plan for getting through birthdays, holidays and anniversaries.
goal: Use it to prepare for hard dates.
body_md: Pick a date and plan how the client wants to spend it, who they want with them and what skills they will use. Include a back-up plan. Review afterward. Expect that feelings vary. Keep the plan flexible.

fields.label: The date I am preparing for
How I would like to spend it
Who I want near
Skills I will use
A back-up plan if it feels like too much

title: Remembering Together Scrapbook
summary: A child and parent make a small scrapbook of pictures and stories about someone who died.
goal: Use it to give a child a safe way to remember.
body_md: The child chooses pictures and draws. The parent listens, shares their own memories and answers questions honestly in simple words. Let the child lead and stop when they want. Keep it somewhere easy to reach.

fields.label: My favorite memory of them
Something they liked
Something I wish I could tell them
How I feel today
Who I can talk to about them

title: Needs and Requests Sheet
summary: A sheet for turning a complaint into a need and a clear, doable request.
goal: Use it to help a client ask for what they want.
body_md: Take a complaint and ask what need sits beneath it. Then turn the need into a specific request. Role play it. Remind the client that the other person may say no. Revise until the request is clear.

fields.label: My complaint
The need underneath it
A specific request
How I will ask
What I will do if the answer is no

title: Relationship Assumption Check
summary: A thought record for assumptions about what a partner or friend means.
goal: Use it to catch mind reading in close relationships.
body_md: Choose a recent exchange and write the assumption. Ask what else it could mean and how the client could check. Practice asking a question. Notice patterns across relationships.

fields.label: What happened
What I assumed
Other explanations
How I could check
What I will say or do

title: Daily Connection Rituals Sheet
summary: A sheet for choosing a few small daily rituals that keep partners connected.
goal: Use it to build everyday connection.
body_md: Each partner suggests rituals, like a morning hug or a goodbye kiss, and the couple picks two to start. Keep them small. Review after a week. They work by being regular, not long.

fields.label: Partner A: rituals I would like
Partner B: rituals I would like
The two we chose
When each will happen
How we will remind each other

title: Relationship Mindfulness Practice
summary: A practice for being fully present with a loved one for a few minutes.
goal: Use it to bring attention and warmth to everyday contact.
body_md: Pick a short window, ten minutes, with no phones. Practice listening and noticing. Debrief what was different. Encourage one or two tries per week. Keep expectations low.

fields.label: When I tried it
What I noticed about the other person
What pulled my attention
How it felt
When I will try again

title: Relationship Tic-Tac-Talk
summary: A tic-tac-toe game where each square holds a communication prompt answered before placing a mark.
goal: Use it to practice talking about relationships in a light way.
body_md: Fill the grid with prompts such as describe a time you felt heard. Players answer before marking. Keep prompts low stakes. Debrief what was easy and hard to say.

fields.label: The prompt I answered
What I said
What I learned from a partner's answer
A prompt that was hard
What I will try with someone I care about

title: Support Circle Map
summary: A map of people and places that offer safety and support, ranked by how safe they feel.
goal: Use it to help a client notice who and what is on their side.
body_md: Keep it entirely about the present. Never ask for details of what happened. Let the client place people closer or further and revisit often. Also include places, pets, routines and professionals. If a minor discloses, follow your reporting duties.

fields.label: People who feel safe to me
Places that feel safe
A routine that helps me feel steady
Someone I want to feel closer to
Someone I will contact this week

title: Self-Blame Gentle Reframe
summary: A gentle sheet for noticing self-blame thoughts and offering a kinder, fairer view.
goal: Use it to ease self-blame without revisiting events.
body_md: Keep the work on current thoughts and never ask for details. Use language that places responsibility with the person who caused harm. Go at the client's pace and stop if it is too much. The client chooses the words that feel true.

fields.label: A self-blaming thought I have
Where I think it came from
What I would say to a friend
A fairer way to see it
Who can support me with this

title: Safe Body Connection Practice
summary: A brief practice for noticing safe, neutral parts of the body and the present moment.
goal: Use it to rebuild a sense of safety in the body at the client's pace.
body_md: Offer choices at every step and make clear that the client can stop at any time. Start with outside of the body, like feet on the floor. Never push. Debrief what felt okay. Stay with the present.

fields.label: A part of my body that feels neutral or okay
What I notice in my feet
What I see in the room
What I want to do if it feels like too much
How I felt afterward

title: Safety Skills Menu
summary: A menu of calming and safety skills for hard moments.
goal: Use it to give a client choices for feeling steadier.
body_md: Build it from what the client already uses and add one or two new ones. Practice a couple in session. Include people to call and, if the client is at risk, call or text 988. Keep the focus on present safety.

fields.label: Skills that help me feel steady
A person to contact
A place I can go
What I will say to myself
If I am in crisis, I can call or text 988

title: Safe Adults Hand Drawing
summary: A child traces a hand and writes a trusted grown-up on each finger, as a plan for who to tell if something feels wrong.
goal: Use it to help a child name safe people they can go to.
body_md: The child traces their hand and writes names. The parent helps pick adults the child can reach. Say clearly that the child can tell and will be believed. Clinicians should remember their reporting duties if a child discloses, and avoid asking leading questions.

fields.label: The first safe grown-up
The second safe grown-up
The third safe grown-up
What I will say if something feels wrong
Where I keep this drawing

title: Coping Strategy Test Drive Sheet
summary: A sheet for trying a coping strategy as an experiment and rating what it does.
goal: Use it to find which skills actually help.
body_md: Pick one skill and a situation and rate distress before and after. Record what was hard about using it. Expect some to fail, which is useful information. Choose what to try next together.

fields.label: The skill I tried
The situation
How I felt before and after
What got in the way
What I will try next

title: Coping Thought Rehearsal Card
summary: A card with coping thoughts for a hard situation that a client rehearses aloud.
goal: Use it to prepare self-talk before it is needed.
body_md: Write coping statements in the client's own voice and rehearse them. Test them against a recent hard moment. Edit anything that sounds fake. Put the card where the client can see it.

fields.label: The hard situation
A coping thought that feels true
Another that feels useful
When I will read the card
What I will do afterward

title: Skill Willingness Check
summary: A check on whether the client is willing to use a skill even when it feels uncomfortable.
goal: Use it to help a client use skills with discomfort present.
body_md: Ask where on a scale the client is willing to try a skill. If low, explore what is in the way. A small willingness is enough. Notice avoidance disguised as coping.

fields.label: A skill I know but do not use
How willing I am, 0 to 10
What is in the way
What would help me try
When I will try it

title: Distress Tolerance Menu Builder
summary: A menu builder for crisis survival skills sorted by situation and intensity.
goal: Use it to give a client options for different moments.
body_md: Sort skills into groups for low, medium and high intensity. Choose one or two for each. Practice them. Revise after use. Keep it handy, such as in a phone note.

fields.label: Skills for low intensity
Skills for medium intensity
Skills for high intensity
A skill I want to learn
Where I keep this menu

title: Coping Skill Charades Relay
summary: A relay in which teams act out coping skills and race to name them.
goal: Use it to refresh coping skills in a lively way.
body_md: Teams line up and take turns acting out skill cards without speaking. Guessers name the skill and say a time they used it. Keep scoring light. Debrief which skills people forgot and which they want to try.

fields.label: A skill I acted or guessed
A time I used it
A skill I forgot
A skill I want to try
What I will remember from today

title: Fear Facts Sheet
summary: A fact sheet a client fills in about their fear: what they know, what they assume and what they could find out.
goal: Use it to separate facts from guesses about a feared thing.
body_md: Ask the client what they know about the feared thing and what they assume. Help them check facts together. Do not argue with the fear. Plan a safe way to gather more information.

fields.label: The thing I fear
What I know for sure
What I assume
How I could find out more
What I notice in my body when I think of it

title: Feared Outcome Probability Check
summary: A check for the predicted outcome of facing a fear, with space for what actually occurred.
goal: Use it to compare predictions with what happens.
body_md: Write the predicted outcome and how sure the client is. Facing it gradually, then record what happened. Discuss the differences. A prediction that came true is information as well. Plan a next step.

fields.label: The feared outcome
How sure I am, 0 to 100
What I did
What happened
What I learned

title: Fear and Freedom Practice
summary: A practice for naming what a fear keeps out of a client's life and one step they are willing to take.
goal: Use it to link exposure steps to something meaningful.
body_md: Ask what the client would be doing if the fear were quieter. Choose a small step toward it and agree to bring the fear along. Debrief afterward.

fields.label: What fear has kept me from
What I would like to be doing
A small step I am willing to take
What the fear says
What I will do with it

title: Exposure Day Skills Plan
summary: A plan of skills to use before, during and after a practice step.
goal: Use it to help a client stay with an exposure step.
body_md: Plan skills for each stage. Remind the client the point is to stay with the step, not to eliminate fear. Practice breathing and grounding. Debrief afterward and celebrate the attempt.

fields.label: Today's step
A skill I will use beforehand
A skill I will use during
How I will reward myself after
What I will review

title: Fear Fighter Superhero Craft
summary: A child designs a superhero costume piece and picks a small brave step to take.
goal: Use it to make facing small fears playful.
body_md: The child decorates a cape or badge and names a power. They choose a tiny brave step with the parent's help. The parent cheers on, never forces and stays near. Repeat with bigger steps later.

fields.label: My superhero name
My power
The fear I am facing
My first small brave step
How my parent will help

title: Body Appreciation Letter Sheet
summary: A letter of thanks to the body for what it does and has carried the client through.
goal: Use it to focus on what the body does rather than how it looks.
body_md: Invite the client to write to their body with thanks. Keep the focus on abilities and experiences. Avoid any talk of size or measurement. Notice discomfort and slow down. Optional to read aloud.

fields.label: Something my body helps me do
A time it carried me through
Something I want to say to it
What I want to do to care for it
How writing this felt

title: Appearance Comparison Thought Check
summary: A thought record for thoughts that compare appearance with others.
goal: Use it to loosen comparison thoughts.
body_md: Look at what the comparison says and where the standard comes from. Ask what is left out of the picture. Move attention toward values. Keep it away from any measuring of the body.

fields.label: The comparison I made
What I told myself
Where this standard came from
What is missing from the picture
What I would rather focus on

title: Values Beyond the Mirror Practice
summary: A practice for acting on what matters when appearance thoughts are loud.
goal: Use it to take values-based actions while thoughts about looks are present.
body_md: Ask what the client has been holding back from because of appearance thoughts. Choose a small step and agree to bring the thoughts along. Debrief on what the experience was.

fields.label: Something I put off because of how I look
Why it matters to me
A small step I will take
What my mind says about it
What I do while it chatters

title: Body Neutral Mindfulness Card
summary: A card for describing the body in neutral, factual words during mindfulness.
goal: Use it to move from judgment toward neutral description.
body_md: Teach describing sensations and functions in neutral words, such as strong legs or warm hands. Practice a short scan. Avoid any evaluation of shape or size. Review what felt possible.

fields.label: A neutral word for my body today
Something it did today
How I noticed the judgment voice
What I did when it came
How I will practice again

title: Body Superpowers Poster
summary: A child draws or collages the things their body can do and displays it as a poster.
goal: Use it to celebrate what the body can do.
body_md: The child draws or cuts pictures of their favorite movements and abilities. The parent talks about what bodies do and avoids appearance comments. Hang the poster in the child's room.

fields.label: A power my body has
Another thing my body can do
A way my body helps my friends
How I take care of my body
What I will add next
